name: Colruyt Group N.V.
reason: Belgian discount grocer with 10y EPS CAGR of only 1.2% (EUR 2.49 in 2015 to 2.80 in 2025), EBIT margin down from 4.7% to 2.6% and consensus FY2-FY3 growth of 3-5%; a cheap but ordinary price-competitive retailer with no route to 7%.

name: Svenska Handelsbanken AB
reason: Conservative, well-run Nordic bank, but EPS barely moved through the zero-rate years (SEK 6.41 in 2016 to 7.91 in 2021), 10y avg ROE is 11.7%, and 2025 EPS of SEK 11.29 is a rate-cycle level with consensus FY1/FY3 of +1%/+4% and LTG 1.4%; fails the bank growth standard.

name: Watches of Switzerland Group PLC
reason: Luxury watch retailer dependent on Rolex/Patek allocations; Rolex's ownership of rival Bucherer is a credible single-supplier threat, EPS of GBP 0.45 (2025) is below the 2022 peak of 0.53 and adjusted EPS runs ~29% above GAAP.

name: CrediaBank S.A.
reason: Former Attica Bank: repeated losses and recapitalisations across 2015-2024 (shares outstanding up ~293%/yr, 10y avg ROE -44.6%) with no meaningful earnings record; a turnaround bank whose earnings rest on Greek credit and rates.

name: ING Bank Slaski S.A.
reason: Good Polish bank (10y avg ROE 16.9%) but EPS rose from PLN 10.28 (2020) to 42.18 (2025) on the rate cycle, consensus FY1 is -24% as rates fall, and Polish bank-tax/CHF-mortgage policy risk persists; earnings set by rates, not forecastable compounding.

name: Industrie De Nora SpA
reason: Leading electrode franchise, but GAAP EPS has swung EUR 0.19-1.52 over 2020-25 (2025: 0.41) on hydrogen/energy-transition project timing and nucera stake effects, with consensus FY1 -19%; only 7 years of history and no reliable route to forecast 5-10y EPS.

name: Swedbank AB
reason: Swedish/Baltic retail bank whose EPS was flat through the zero-rate years (SEK 17.50 in 2016 to 18.56 in 2021) and jumped to 28.98-30.86 only on the rate cycle; 10y EPS CAGR 7.2% is rate-driven and FY1 consensus is -4%, so it fails the through-cycle bank standard.

name: Pharma Mar SA
reason: Single-franchise oncology biotech (Zepzelca/Yondelis royalties) with EBIT margin swinging -21% to +58% and EPS EUR 7.49 (2020) to 0.06 (2023) to 4.30 (2025); earnings depend on licensing milestones and trial outcomes and cannot be forecast.

name: Volvo AB
reason: High-quality truck and construction-equipment OEM (10y avg ROE 21.7%), but EPS is set by the freight/truck cycle (SEK 24.78 in 2024 to 16.94 in 2025, -46% in 2020) and emissions-transition capex; consistent with PACCAR, quality but not forecastable 5-10y.

name: Associated British Foods plc
reason: Primark plus a commodity sugar/agriculture arm: 10y EPS CAGR 5.5% (GBP 1.02 to 1.75), sugar profits swing with EU prices, consensus FY1 -12% and FY2 -4%, and adjusted EPS runs ~22% above GAAP; no clear route to 7%.

name: Grenergy Renovables S.A
reason: Renewables developer whose EPS (EUR 3.08 in 2025) comes from building and selling solar/storage projects, with FCF yield -36.6%, FCF conversion -6.7x and net debt/EBITDA 5.2x; growth is financed by leverage and asset rotation.

name: Allianz SE
reason: Well-run diversified insurer with 10y avg ROE 12.6% and shares -1.7%/yr, but EPS was flat through the zero-rate years (EUR 15.05 in 2016 to 15.83 in 2021) and 2025 EPS of 28.61 is a 10y high driven by hard P&C pricing, higher yields and PIMCO flows; consistent with TRV/HIG, we cannot tell how much is cycle.

name: Avarda Bank AB
reason: Former TF Bank with an excellent record (EPS SEK 2.06 to 9.96 over 2016-25, 8/9 years up, 10y avg ROE 26%), but earnings come from unsecured consumer lending and BNPL in Germany/Nordics that has not been tested in a credit downturn, plus the recent Avarda integration; credit-cycle risk makes 5-10y EPS unforecastable.

name: KWS SAAT SE & Co KGaA
reason: Durable family-controlled seed breeder, but 10y EPS CAGR is 6.6% (EUR 2.51 to 4.88), consensus FY1-FY3 growth is 4.5-5.4% with LTG 2%, and FCF conversion is only 0.26; good but no route to 7% growth.

name: AAK AB
reason: Specialty vegetable oils and fats (chocolate, bakery, infant nutrition) sold through a co-development model with cost pass-through: 10y EPS CAGR 13.4% (SEK 3.75 to 13.16), 6/10 years at or above 7%, avg ROIC 12.8%, net debt/EBITDA 0.64x and consensus FY2-FY3 of about 8%; the deep dive must test the 91st-pctile margin (9.7% vs 7.5% avg) and weak 0.32 FCF conversion.

name: British Land Company PLC
reason: London office/retail REIT with FFO per share flat to down (GBP 0.47 in FY2016 to 0.29 in FY2025), 10y revenue CAGR -1.2%, net debt/EBITDA 10.8x and consensus FY1-FY3 growth of 4-6%; property-cycle earner with no route to 7%.

name: ROCKWOOL A/S
reason: Stone-wool insulation leader with an energy-efficiency tailwind, but earnings are tied to the construction cycle, the EBIT margin of 14.7% is at the 91st pctile, and the adjusted EPS series is broken in 2025 (0.13 vs 2.57, consensus FY1 +1291%), so the base cannot be normalised.

name: Television Francaise 1 SA
reason: French free-to-air broadcaster facing structural decline in linear TV advertising to streaming: 10y revenue CAGR 1.4%, EPS EUR 0.75 in 2025 below the 2021 high of 1.09, and consensus FY1 -40%.

name: Van Lanschot Kempen NV
reason: Private bank and asset manager whose earnings follow capital markets (EPS -47% in 2020, EUR 3.64 in 2025 at its 10y high on AUM and investment-banking fees), with 10y avg ROE 7.6% and consensus FY2-FY3 of 6-7%; fails the wealth-manager rule.

name: Standard Life plc
reason: Closed-book life consolidator (formerly Phoenix): IFRS EPS swings (GBP -0.86 in 2021 to 0.54 in 2025), shares +13%/yr from acquisitions, 10y avg ROE -16% and earnings sensitive to markets and rates; acquisition-led and hard to forecast.
